topic_ko: 웃음이 있고 없고에 따라 농담의 평가가 달라진다는 실험 — 웃음의 사회성·전염성

passage: Researchers played a series of weak jokes to 72 listeners.
Each joke was followed by silence, by pretend laughter, or by genuine laughter.
Listeners then scored how amusing each joke seemed to them.
Jokes met with silence scored lowest of all.
Pretend laughter lifted the scores by about a tenth.
Genuine laughter lifted them by roughly a fifth.
So what we hear around a joke shapes how funny the joke feels.
Laughter, it seems, spreads between people and draws them closer.
choices: the techniques comedians use to write more effective jokes
why some listeners are harder to amuse than others
how the laughter surrounding a joke changes our judgment of it
the health benefits that regular laughter brings to the body
how researchers design experiments with large numbers of subjects
theme.explanation_ko: 웃음이 없을 때·가짜일 때·진짜일 때 농담 점수가 달라졌고, 결론은 웃음이 사람 사이에 퍼져 농담의 평가를 바꾼다는 것이므로 ③이 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 농담을 쓰는 기법은 다루지 않는다. ② 개인차는 언급되지 않았다. ④ 웃음의 건강 효과는 이 글에 없다. ⑤ 실험 설계 방법론이 아니라 결과의 의미가 초점이다.

passage: In one study, 72 people listened to a set of corny jokes.
After each joke came either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter.
The listeners rated how funny they found every joke.
Jokes that landed in silence received poor ratings.
Fake laughter raised the rating by ten percent.
Real laughter raised it by twenty percent.
Both kinds of laughter therefore changed how funny the jokes seemed.
We judge a joke partly by the response it receives from others.
choices: 농담의 완성도가 높을수록 청중의 웃음도 커진다.
실험 참가자의 수가 많을수록 결과의 신뢰도가 높아진다.
농담의 재미는 그 농담이 받는 웃음이라는 반응에 크게 좌우된다.
유머 감각은 타고나는 것이 아니라 훈련으로 길러진다.
진짜 웃음과 가짜 웃음은 청중에게 전혀 다르게 인식된다.
gist.explanation_ko: 웃음이 없으면 점수가 낮고 가짜·진짜 웃음이 붙으면 점수가 올랐다는 결과에서, 농담의 재미가 반응에 좌우된다는 ③이 요지이다.
gist.distractor_ko: ⑤ 둘 다 점수를 올렸으므로 "전혀 다르게"는 틀리다. ① 농담의 완성도는 통제된 변수였다. ② 표본 크기 논의는 없다. ④ 유머 감각의 습득은 다루지 않는다.

passage: Seventy-two volunteers sat and listened to a run of dad jokes.
Some jokes were followed by nothing, some by forced laughter, some by real laughter.
The volunteers scored each joke for how funny it was.
Silence produced the lowest scores.
Forced laughter added ten percent to the score.
Real laughter added twenty percent.
Hearing others laugh readies us to laugh along.
That is why laughter both sharpens a joke and binds a room together.
choices: Why a Joke Gets Funnier When Someone Else Laughs
The Lost Art of Writing a Perfect Punchline
Measuring Intelligence Through a Sense of Humor
How Comedians Train Audiences to Respond on Cue
Silence: The Most Powerful Tool in Comedy
title.explanation_ko: 남의 웃음을 들으면 따라 웃을 준비가 되어 농담이 더 웃겨진다는 것이 글의 핵심이므로 ①이 제목으로 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ② 농담 작법은 다루지 않는다. ③ 지능과의 관련은 없다. ④ 청중을 훈련시키는 이야기가 아니다. ⑤ 침묵은 점수가 가장 낮은 조건이었을 뿐 도구로 예찬되지 않는다.

passage: A study asked 72 people to rate a set of weak jokes.
Some jokes were followed by silence, others by fake or real laughter.
Jokes that drew no laughter were rated poorly.
Fake laughter pushed ratings up ten percent, real laughter twenty.
This is because we get ready to smile or laugh when we hear someone else laughing.
It is fair to say that a joke, in other words, never really lands alone.
implication.underlined: a joke, in other words, never really lands alone
choices: jokes are only successful when the listener already knows the speaker
the meaning of a joke changes each time it is told to someone new
a joke must be repeated several times before an audience accepts it
comedians should avoid performing in front of very small groups
how funny a joke seems depends on the reactions of the people around us
implication.explanation_ko: 밑줄은 농담이 홀로 평가되지 않는다는 뜻으로, 앞에서 제시한 "주변의 웃음이 평가를 바꾼다"는 결과를 압축한 표현이다. 따라서 ⑤가 함축 의미이다.
implication.distractor_ko: ③ 반복은 언급되지 않는다. ④ 청중 규모 이야기가 아니다. ① 화자와의 친분은 나오지 않는다. ② 농담의 의미 변화가 아니라 재미의 평가가 초점이다.

passage: In a scientific study, 72 people were asked to listen to a set of dad jokes.
Following each joke came either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter.
Every participant then rated how funny the jokes were.
Jokes followed by fake laughter were rated ten percent funnier than silent ones.
This study shows that both real and fake laughter makes a big difference.
It suggests that we pay attention not just to the content but also to the reaction.
This is because we get ready to laugh when we hear someone else laughing.
Laughter not only makes jokes funnier but also brings people together.

underlines.text: either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter

choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
grammar.explanation_ko: both A and B 가 주어이면 복수 취급이므로 makes 가 아니라 make 여야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① ask + O + to V 의 수동태로 적절하다. ② either 는 or 와 짝을 이루며 세 항목으로 확장될 수 있다. ③ 간접의문문은 「의문사+주어+동사」 어순이다. ⑤ not only A but also B 에서 앞의 makes 와 형태가 일치한다.

passage: In a scientific study, 72 people listened to a series of dad jokes.
After each joke there was no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter.
The participants then rated how funny the jokes were.
Jokes with no laughter did not receive high ratings.
Jokes followed by fake laughter were rated ten percent funnier.
This shows that both kinds of laughter make a big difference to our judgment.
It suggests that we ignore the reaction a joke gets from other people.
Laughter makes jokes funnier and also brings people together.
choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
vocab.explanation_ko: 실험은 우리가 반응에 세심한 주의를 기울인다는 것을 보여 주므로 ignore(무시하다)는 정반대다. notice 나 pay attention to 가 되어야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① 세 조건 중 하나로 fake 가 맞다. ② 점수를 매겼으므로 rated 가 적절하다. ③ 비교 대상이 있으므로 비교급 funnier 가 맞다. ⑤ 웃음이 사람을 이어 준다는 결론과 일치한다.

passage: A study had 72 people listen to a set of dad jokes.
Each joke was followed by silence, by fake laughter, or by real laughter.
Jokes that met silence were rated lowest.
Fake laughter raised the ratings ten percent, and real laughter twenty percent.
Even laughter the listeners knew was not sincere still worked.
What mattered, then, was ______________________.
Hearing anyone laugh prepares us to laugh as well.
choices: how sincere the laughter sounded to the listener
whether the joke had been written by a professional
how long the listeners had known one another
simply that laughter was present at all
the exact number of people in the room
blank.explanation_ko: 진짜가 아닌 가짜 웃음조차 점수를 올렸다는 앞 문장이 근거다. 중요한 것은 웃음의 진위가 아니라 웃음이 있었다는 사실 자체이므로 ④가 적절하다.
blank.distractor_ko: ② 농담의 작성자는 언급되지 않는다. ③ 참가자들의 친분은 나오지 않는다. ⑤ 인원수는 72명으로 고정된 조건이다. ① 가짜 웃음도 효과가 있었으므로 진정성은 결정적 요인이 아니다.

order.given: In a scientific study, 72 people were asked to listen to a series of dad jokes. After each joke, there was either no laughter, fake laughter, or real laughter, and the participants then rated how funny the jokes were.

blocks.A: The pattern was clear. Jokes that were met with silence did not earn high ratings from the listeners at all.
blocks.B: Laughter that everyone knew was fake still raised the ratings by ten percent, and real laughter raised them by twenty percent.
blocks.C: This suggests that we attend not only to a joke itself but also to the response it draws, because hearing others laugh readies us to laugh too.

order.explanation_ko: 결과의 도입(A) → 구체적 수치(B) → 해석과 결론(C) 순서가 자연스럽다.
order.distractor_ko: C 는 해석이므로 수치보다 앞설 수 없고, B 의 "still" 은 A 의 침묵 조건과 대비되어야 하므로 A 가 B 보다 앞선다.

insert.insert_sentence: Remarkably, laughter the participants knew to be fake still had an effect.

passage: In a scientific study, 72 people rated a series of dad jokes.
Each joke was followed by silence, by fake laughter, or by real laughter.
Silence produced the lowest ratings of all.
Fake laughter raised ratings by ten percent and real laughter by twenty.
Hearing someone else laugh prepares us to smile or laugh ourselves.
Laughter therefore makes jokes funnier and also brings people together.
summary.explanation_ko: 가짜든 진짜든 웃음이 "있다"는 사실만으로 점수가 올랐으므로 (A)는 presence, 웃음이 사람을 이어 준다고 했으므로 (B)는 social 이다.
summary.distractor_ko: (A) quality·length 는 웃음의 질이나 길이를 비교한 것이 아니므로 부적절하다. (B) private·logical 은 글의 결론(사회적·전염적)과 반대이거나 무관하다.
summary.summary_template: The experiment showed that the mere __(A)__ of laughter, whether genuine or not, made jokes seem funnier, which reveals the __(B)__ nature of laughter.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 진짜 웃음과 가짜 웃음 둘 다 큰 차이를 만든다.
writing.answer: Both real and fake laughter make a big difference.
writing.explanation_ko: both A and B 가 주어이면 복수 취급이므로 동사는 make 이다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 웃음은 농담을 더 웃기게 만들 뿐만 아니라 사람들을 이어 주기도 한다.
conditions: not only ~ but also 를 사용할 것
writing.answer: Laughter not only makes jokes funnier but also brings people together.
writing.explanation_ko: not only A but also B 는 같은 형태를 연결하므로 makes 와 brings 가 짝을 이룬다.

writing.question: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.context: Because even laughter that the listeners knew was not genuine still raised the ratings, the study suggests that laughter is ___________ — it spreads from one person to another.
writing.explanation_ko: 남이 웃으면 따라 웃을 준비를 하게 된다는 설명에 해당하므로 contagious(전염성의)가 적절하다. (infectious 도 가능)

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.context: It suggests that we pay close attention not just to a joke’s content but also to the reaction it gets.
writing.answer: 이는 우리가 농담의 내용뿐만 아니라 그것이 받는 반응에도 세심한 주의를 기울인다는 것을 시사한다.
writing.explanation_ko: not just A but also B 가 전치사구끼리 병렬을 이루고, the reaction 뒤에 목적격 관계대명사가 생략되어 있다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.explanation_ko: 웃음이 사람들을 이어 주므로 social, 남의 웃음이 내 웃음을 유발하므로 contagious 이다.
writing.summary: The study found that both fake and real laughter made jokes seem funnier, showing that laughter is __(A)__ and __(B)__ rather than a purely private response.

writing.question: 본문의 주제를 한 문장의 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 농담의 재미는 그것이 받는 웃음이라는 반응에 크게 좌우된다.
writing.answer: How funny a joke seems depends largely on the laughter it receives.
writing.explanation_ko: 간접의문문 How funny a joke seems 를 주어로 두고 depend on 으로 연결한다.
